text:
maria-platts: noticed a p99 spike on hosted-api starting ~02:10 UTC, p99 ~1.9s vs baseline ~420ms. p50/p95 fine. https://grafana.redwood/hosted-api/d/p99

- looks correlated with increased queue depth on inference workers

Derek: what changed around 02:00-02:10? any deploys or config flips?

maria-platts: we rolled dynamic kernel-selector (kselector) to 100% at 02:05 to optimize kernel choices by seq_len distribution. also pulled runtime kvcache eviction tuning PR earlier in the day (PR #1542).

deploy-bot: deploy finished: kselector-rollout @02:05 UTC (commit b7c3f9). canary -> prod.

anthony: grabbing quick profiler traces from one affected worker. nvprof shows memcpy stalls and a lot of small kernel launches when requests have mixed seq lengths. snippet:
```
GPU time by API:
  memcpy HtoD: 28.4%
  memcpy DtoH: 12.1%
  kernel launches (small): 45.0% (many < 200us)
  kernel compute heavy paths: 14.5%
```
looks like frequent kernel switching causing metadata work + small launches.

rachel: infra metrics: kselector.swap_count per-host jumped x3 after rollout; kvcache.evictions spiked ~5x for the same hosts. also queue_depth 95th moved from 2 -> 8.

sre-jen: do we have request traces? sample request ids & model variants?

maria-platts: sample ids in logs: req=hosted-req-20260318-4912, hosted-req-20260318-4931. sequences vary 8->1024 tokens in same batch window. pasted a short log: 
```
[02:09:45] req hosted-req-4912 seq=24 batch=3 kernel=fast_fp16
[02:09:45] req hosted-req-4931 seq=1024 batch=1 kernel=slow_int8
[02:09:46] kselector: swap kernel fast_fp16 -> slow_int8 (cost_estimate diff 0.12)
[02:09:46] kvcache: evict prefix tenant=acct-998 count=6
```
Derek: hypothesis: dynamic selector swapping kernels mid-workload causes mixed kernel launches, which increases per-request latency and causes KV cache churn because sequence priming behavior changes. noisy sequences (large seq) force fallback kernels and evict prefetched KV entries.

anthony: quick mitigation we can test: revert kselector to conservative/static selection for prod (no on-the-fly swaps) or throttle swaps when batch_variance > 0.4. small patch to set threshold: `kselector.swap_threshold = 0.6`

maria-platts: can we flip a runtime flag without full rollback?

deploy-bot: runtime config toggle available: `kselector.mode` accepts `dynamic|conservative|static`. current=dynamic.

Derek: flip to `conservative` on the 6 affected clusters first. conservative should prefer a stable kernel for a short window (30s) to avoid swap thrash.

ops-bot: starting config update on hosted-prod-us-west-2 -> kselector.mode=conservative (rolling).

anthony: while toggling, I captured a flamegraph showing many small kernels due to seq variance. adding link: https://perf.redwood/trace/2951234567-flame

rachel: after toggle: observing p99 back to ~450ms within 90s on updated hosts. queue_depth 95th falling back to 2. kvcache.evictions dropping to baseline.

maria-platts: confirmed across all host pools in prod, p99 near baseline. thanks team. :tada:

sre-jen: follow-ups:
- create issue to add unit/integration test that simulates mixed seq_len batches and ensures kselector avoids frequent swaps
- add a guard on swap logic to check `predicted_swap_benefit > swap_cost + eviction_penalty`
- instrument per-tenant kvcache-prefetch hit/miss counters in the canary dashboard

Derek: I'll open the rollback/patch PR to change default mode to conservative and add a feature flag. PR draft link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1604

anthony: also adding a small perf regression test harness that fuzzes seq_len distribution and measures kernel launch overhead; will add to CI.

maria-platts: noted. creating incident doc and linking this thread. we should schedule a post-mortem to decide whether dynamic mode needs more safety checks before a global rollout.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-03-18-5821. assigned to eng-runtime.

Derek: thanks all — great quick collaboration.
